previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and a chronic left hip pressure ulcer, was admitted for generalized weakness and fever initially suspected to be a urinary tract infection. However, urine culture was negative, and elevated inflammatory markers along with imaging findings raised concern for osteomyelitis. A bone biopsy was performed, and wound culture grew MRSA, leading to a diagnosis of acute osteomyelitis of the left ischium. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral doxycycline. Due to ongoing wound care needs, malnutrition, and limited home support, he was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation, wound management, and antibiotic completion. His multiple sclerosis and depression were managed supportively during admission.

radiology_notes.text:
RADIOGRAPHS OF THE PELVIS AND LEFT HIP

HISTORY:  History of left hip osteomyelitis.  Question progression. 
Background multiple sclerosis.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Left hip, two views, and AP pelvis, two views.

FINDINGS:  A stimulator device is in place.  Staples and clips again project
over the lower pelvis and the scrotum.  The bones appear demineralized. 
Moderate degenerative changes involve each hip joint.  There is a soft tissue
defect that appears to probe to the greater trochanter of the left proximal
femur.  There is new but slight irregular sclerosis along the margins.  

IMPRESSION:  Slight sclerosis which may reflect chronic osteomyelitis in the
appropriate clinical setting.  If further assessment is needed, an MR could be
considered.

CHEST RADIOGRAPHS

HISTORY:  Cough and fever.  History of smoking.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest, AP semi-upright..

FINDINGS:  The cardiac, mediastinal and hilar contours appear stable.  There
is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Aside from small calcified granulomas
in each lung, Tthe lungs appear otherwise clear.  The patient is status post
incompletely characterized anterior lower cervical fusion.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute disease.

INDICATION:  ___ man with pseudomonas UTI/bacteremia, needs two week
course of IV antibiotics.  Please place bedside PICC.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ (radiology fellow) and Dr. ___
___ (radiology attending) who was present throughout and supervised the
procedure.

RADIATION:  2.3 minutes fluoroscopy time, 2 mGy.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

The patient was brought to the angiographic suite and placed supine on the
table.  A preprocedure timeout was performed using three patient identifiers. 
Multiple previous attempts had been made to access the right arm veins and had
not succeeded; therefore, we attempted to access the left-sided veins.  The
skin of the left upper extremity was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.  A tourniquet was applied to the upper arm.  Initial ultrasound
confirmed patency of the left basilic vein.  Approximately 1 cc of 1%
lidocaine was infiltrated into the skin and subcutaneous tissues.  Using
ultrasound guidance, a micropuncture needle was advanced into the left basilic
vein.  Ultrasound images were saved prior to and after venipuncture confirming
patency of the vein.  A nitinol wire was advanced through the needle without
difficulty, this passed readily into the central veins, right atrium and IVC. 
A small skin incision was made.  The needle was removed and exchanged for a
4.5 ___ peel-away sheath.  A single-lumen Power PICC was flushed and cut to
an appropriate length of 48 cm.  This was then advanced over the wire.  The
peel-away sheath was gradually removed and the catheter was advanced.  The
wire was then removed.  Following this maneuver the tip of the catheter was in
the distal SVC.  The catheter aspirated and flushed without difficulty.  A
StatLock device was used to secure the catheter and a sterile dressing was
applied.  There were no immediate post-procedure complications.

IMPRESSION:  Technically successful placement of a left basilic single-lumen
Power PICC. The catheter has been flushed and is ready for use, the tip is in
the distal SVC.
